accuracy.evidence: All numbers were computed, not estimated: 1.15^(1/12) = 1.011715 (shown as 1.0117, about 1.17% a month), 1.0125^12 = 1.1608, 1.01^12 = 1.126825, 2^(1/3) = 1.2599, 2^(1/5) = 1.1487, 0.5^(1/8) = 0.9170, 1.2^(1/4) = 1.0466 and 1.15^2 = 1.3225. The identity a^t = (a^(1/n))^(nt) = (a^k)^(t/k) is stated as the law that changes the period without changing the function, matching the A-level indices and exponential modelling content.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the standard compounding errors: dividing an annual rate by 12 (the 1.0125 trap in steps 1 and 4, challenge tag div), multiplying a monthly rate by 12 (tag mul), adding 15% + 15% for two years (the 1.30^(t/2) card, tag add), squaring the rate instead of the factor (tag sq), changing the exponent but not the base (the 1.15^(12t) card, tag same) and reading a doubling time as 2 divided by k (tag exp).

lab_distinct.evidence: flag_rexp.js is about changing the period of an exponential, not about starting values or graph shapes: a monthly-factor slider with twelve compounding bars against a ×1.15 target, a twelve-cell month-by-month compounder, a doubling-law curve read at t = 1, 3 and 6, a same-function sort of six rewritten forms, and a rate-to-any-period converter on one fixed curve. It passed the 30% shingle gate against flaggrow, flagexpg, flagreveal and every other flag lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each task is one move from the topic statement: finding m with m^12 = 1.15 is the 1.15^t to 1.0117^(12t) rewrite; compounding twelve months is the reverse; reading 2^(t/3) at t = 1 turns a doubling time into a yearly factor; the sort checks equivalence with the power law; the converter shows the factor and exponent change while the dots stay on the same curve.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions, each with the wrong answer most students give first: '15 ÷ 12 = 1.25%' for the monthly rate, 'exactly 12%' for 1% a month, '2 ÷ 3, about 67%' for 2^(t/3), 'Yes: 15% ÷ 12 a month' for 1.0125^(12t), and '20% + 20% = 40%' over 2 years. Each is tested on the canvas and the reveal gives the computed value.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Four question types with varying rates (15, 8, 20, 12, 6%; 1, 2, 0.5, 1.5% a month; doubling times 3 to 10 years). Every wrong option is tagged (div, mul, same, exp, add, sq) with a specific message, e.g. 'Dividing the rate ignores compounding. Take the root of the factor: a^(1/n).' Choice order rotates each round.

readability.evidence: Learner audience: the learner paragraphs use short sentences, one worked number per sentence, and pass the FK target; the adult paragraphs pass the 10.0 target and set out scope, both directions of the method, the named mistakes and a lab tour. On the canvas each step's equation is written out in full with the current factor and percentage beside it.

no_filler.evidence: No filler phrases (gate passed). Every learner sentence states a rule or a computed value, e.g. '1% a month gives 1.01^12 ≈ 1.1268, so 12.68% a year, not 12%'. Hints give the next operation ('Square the growth factor, do not double the rate') rather than general advice.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 (390 px) screenshots in light and dark for every step before and after Show me. After the first pass the compounding bars were rescaled so the ×1.15 target sits high in the panel, and the converter curve was given a fitted y-range so its curvature shows. Month cells, the three answer cards, the six form cards and both bins fit without clipping; control buttons wrap onto two rows.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button twin (±0.0005 and ±0.0001 for m, Next month, the three yearly forms, t ± 1, Same / Not the same for the next card, ±1% and four period buttons); the canvas aria-label is updated with every message and the current values. Correctness is stated in words. axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) found no violations in light or dark on every step, before and after Show me.
